title: ck says /k/
parentNote: This is the third way to write a sound your child has had for a while: c said /k/, then k said /k/, and today ck says /k/ as well — one pop, not two. The place is what tells you which one to use, and it is worth saying out loud: ck only ever turns up at the END of a short word, right after the little vowel, and never at the start. The mistake to listen for is sounding both letters, so "pick" comes out "pi-cuh-kuh"; cover the k with your finger, read it, then uncover it and read it again exactly the same way. Today is also the day stories start. Three or four lines is a lot of reading held together at once, so read the whole thing to them first, then let them have it — and if they run out of steam, the questions can wait for the second go.

activities.mouthCue: Exactly the same back-of-the-tongue pop as c and k. Two letters on the page, one job for your mouth.

Same start, same ending. Listen hard to the middle.

Both start the same. Does it end at the back of your mouth or at your teeth?
